candidates.attacker_control: The whole archive stream is attacker-controlled (web/api ApplicationsWebResource.installApp: POST /onos/v1/applications with application/octet-stream body, or the JSON variant that fetches a URL; historically also the GUI upload endpoint /rs/applications/upload and the `onos:app install` CLI). ZIP entry names, the app.xml `name`/`featuresRepo` attributes and the features.xml `feature.bundle` value are all taken from the archive without validation of path characters.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The isTopLevel() filter exists but only checks file names, not directories, and `file.isDirectory()` is false for not-yet-created files — it does not prevent traversal. Searched the snapshot for getCanonicalPath/normalize/simplifyPath/path-prefix checks: none are present in archive extraction code. Considered that the concrete ApplicationStore implementation (core/store/dist) is absent from the snapshot, so the final caller could not be inspected in-tree; considered that ONOS administrators can already install apps (which is code execution by design), so the incremental impact is writing outside the application directory/tampering with existing deployment files rather than 'arbitrary code as the ONOS user' alone; considered that plain-XML archives take the expandPlainApplication() path instead.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file creation/overwrite on the controller host with attacker-chosen bytes, restricted only by the name-suffix filter (.jar / *features.xml / app.xml). This crosses the intended per-application sandbox and reaches deployment artifacts (e.g. Karaf `system/` repository jars, other apps' bundles/descriptors, scripts/configuration), enabling persistence or code execution when a tampered bundle is next loaded (restart/bundle refresh), and corruption of other installed applications. Because the same method also builds paths from the archive-supplied app name, directory traversal via app.xml is possible as well.
candidates.prerequisites: Ability to submit an application archive to the install path (in this code base the REST paths are protected by BASIC auth with role `admin` in web/api/WEB-INF/web.xml, and the CLI requires ONOS shell access), plus write permission of the ONOS JVM user at the targeted location. The crafted entry must satisfy isTopLevel(), i.e. be exactly `app.xml`, end with `features.xml` or `.jar` — sufficient to overwrite/replace bundles and descriptors in the deployment.
candidates.root_cause: ApplicationArchive.expandZippedApplication() expands an untrusted ZIP/OAR/JAR stream by computing `File file = new File(appDir, entry.getName())` (line 361) and then calling `createParentDirs(file)` + `Files.write(data, file)` (363-364) without resolving/canonicalizing the path and verifying that it remains under `appDir` (= apps/<appName>, line 356). The only guard, isTopLevel(file) (376-379), checks only the trailing file name (`app.xml`, `*.features.xml`, `*.jar`, or an already-existing directory) and never checks the parent path, so entries such as `../../<dir>/name.jar`, `../../<dir>/features.xml` or an absolute-looking name with `..` segments are accepted and written outside the intended directory. The same unsanitized metadata is reused elsewhere: `saveApplication(InputStream)` (191-222) and `saveApplication(...,desc,...)` (437-442) build paths from the archive-supplied app.xml `name` attribute via appFile() (501-503), and stageSelfContainedJar() (383-409) builds a file path from the archive-supplied `feature.bundle` coordinates.
candidates.title: Path traversal (Zip Slip) in application archive installation — files can be written outside the app directory
candidates.trace: web/api ApplicationsWebResource.installApp(InputStream) (lines 128-144) -> ApplicationAdminService.install(InputStream) -> core/net ApplicationManager.install (147-152) -> ApplicationStore.create(stream) [the concrete distributed ApplicationStore implementation lives in the core/store/dist module, which is not present in this snapshot, but core/store/pom.xml still declares <module>dist</module>] -> ApplicationArchive.saveApplication(InputStream) (191-222) -> expandZippedApplication (349-372): line 356 `new File(appsDir, desc.name())`, line 361 `new File(appDir, entry.getName())`, lines 363-364 `createParentDirs(file); write(data, file)`. With entry name like `../../karaf/system/<bundle>.jar` (or `..... /features.xml`) the File resolves outside apps/<appName> and is created/written by the ONOS process.
candidates.unverified: The concrete ApplicationStore implementation that calls saveApplication (core/store/dist) is missing from the snapshot, so end-to-end reachability from the REST endpoint was established by interface/contract and pom evidence, not by an unbroken in-repo call chain. Not runtime-verified; no exploit executed. Whether a later upstream revision added containment checks is unknown from the snapshot. The features-dir path (stageSelfContainedJar using feature.bundle coordinates) was also not exercised/verified beyond source reading.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal' / 'Zip Slip'); CWE-73 External Control of File Name or Path

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned 8,032-file ONOS 1.14.0-SNAPSHOT via list/search/read plus the P1 relation index (77,580 symbols, 199,064 calls, 152,189 edges; index status complete, no SAST or dataflow claims). Priority coverage: web/api and app REST resources, web/gui and web/gui2 web.xml auth configuration, application installation and archive handling (core/common ApplicationArchive, core/net ApplicationManager, web/api ApplicationsWebResource), YANG compiler/runtime (apps/yang), command-execution sinks (YangLiveCompilerManager, DiagnosticsWebResource, ClusterIpManager), TLS/trust configuration, deserialization (Kryo/readObject), and a sample of app stores/utilities. Not all 8,032 files were read line-by-line; low-risk areas (many drivers, pipelines, GUI JS/TS, packet codecs) were surveyed only by pattern searches. The relation index is navigation-only and was not treated as a vulnerability oracle.
limitations: No tests are present in the snapshot (no src/test directories), so fix-verification tests and expected-behavior tests could not be consulted.

core/store/dist is declared as a module in core/store/pom.xml but its sources are absent from the snapshot; consequently the concrete ApplicationStore implementation that invokes ApplicationArchive.saveApplication (and other core distributed stores such as FlowRuleStore/HostStore implementations) could not be inspected, so the final leg of the install call chain is inferred rather than traced.
No code was executed, no build was run, and no exploit payload was created; all conclusions are static source review.

The P1 relation index provides syntactic/navigation candidates only and explicitly does not prove runtime reachability, complete data flow, or exploitability; index facts were verified against source text where used.

Deployment-time exposure of optional app WABs (e.g. VTN, kafka-integration, PCE, RESTCONF proxy) could not be confirmed from the snapshot, so their missing auth constraints are reported only as rejected/unconfirmed leads.
Binary-like files are refused/skipped by the tools; none were reported as skipped in the searches performed.
Line numbers refer to the assigned snapshot revision and may differ from upstream ONOS.

rejected_leads.lead: Zip Slip in the YANG live compiler: apps/yang/src/main/java/org/onosproject/yang/impl/YangLiveCompilerManager.java extractZipArchive (118-131, sink line 125 `new File(dir, entry.getName())`) — same weakness class as the reported candidate, reached via the `onos:compile-model <modelId> <url>` CLI (YangCompileCommand lines 55-78) and via the source-present but non-built REST module apps/yang/web (no pom.xml; POST /models with no security-constraint in its web.xml).
rejected_leads.reason: Same root-cause family as the selected candidate, so it is not reported separately; in this snapshot its remote endpoint is not part of the Maven build (apps/yang/web has no pom.xml and is not referenced by any aggregator) and the live path requires authenticated CLI access, making its in-snapshot reachability weaker than the core app installer.

rejected_leads.lead: TLS certificate/hostname verification explicitly disabled: apps/openstacknetworking OpenstackNetworkingUtil.java (385-396), apps/openstacknode OpenstackNodeUtil.java (167-178), protocols/rest/api HttpSBControllerImpl.java (285-300), providers/rest/device RestDeviceProviderUtilities.java (48-62).
rejected_leads.reason: Real MITM exposure of controller-to-provider REST/Keystone traffic, but the endpoints are administrator-configured, the code carries explicit FIXMEs, and no untrusted-input boundary is established from source alone.

rejected_leads.lead: Application sub-webapps with no BASIC-auth security-constraint: apps/vtn/vtnweb web.xml (constraint commented out with TODO), apps/kafka-integration, apps/pce/pcerest, protocols/restconf/server/rpp, apps/openstacknetworkingui. These expose REST/JAX-RS endpoints without a declared auth constraint.
rejected_leads.reason: Unverified deployment reachability: these are optional app WABs, several are deprecated/not in the default app set, and no in-snapshot code proves they are exposed on the default listener; kept as a coverage note, not a candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Server-side request forgery / arbitrary URL fetch in ApplicationsWebResource.installApp(String) (web/api lines 95-117: new URL(jsonTree.get(URL).asText()).openStream()).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires administrator REST authentication, and install-from-URL is the documented purpose of the endpoint; the security delta is not comparable to the filename/path traversal issue.

rejected_leads.lead: Argument injection through ComponentConfig values in apps/cip ClusterIpManager.addIpAlias (lines 155-160: `sudo ifconfig` string built from aliasIp/aliasMask/aliasAdapter and passed to Runtime.exec(String)).
rejected_leads.reason: Runtime.exec(String) does not invoke a shell, so shell metacharacters are inert; the values are administrator-set component configuration, and only argument injection/config-side effects are plausible.

rejected_leads.lead: Unauthenticated classpath resource loading with path parameter in web/gui FooResource.getBinResource (lines 75-92: getResourceAsStream("/raw/" + resource)) and unauthenticated read-only GUI /rs/* resources.
rejected_leads.reason: Traversal through class-loader resource lookup is constrained by the classpath/JAR layout and the impact is at most resource disclosure; no sensitive file read path demonstrated.

rejected_leads.lead: Stored/self-XSS in web/gui MainIndexResource (lines 97-133): userName and UI preference JSON are interpolated unescaped into an inline <script> (including the onosAuth websocket token); UiPreferencesWebResource PUT /ui/preferences/{user}/{pref} (web/api lines 103-113) writes values for any named user.
rejected_leads.reason: The REST API requires the admin role and the preference owner is the same authenticated principal in normal use; the XSS is self-targeted and the impact overlaps with privileges an admin already has. Not as strong as the archive path traversal.

rejected_leads.lead: XML parsers without DTD/external-entity hardening (e.g. apps/odtn/api YangToolUtil.toDocument lines 196-218 DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance()), potential XXE.
rejected_leads.reason: Input sources are ODTN CLI/NETCONF/device data rather than a clearly remote untrusted channel; entities/paths not traced to an attacker-controlled boundary. Several other parsers in the tree do disable DTDs, which suggests awareness, but no exploit path was established.

rejected_leads.lead: Class.forName(request.getComponentClass()) in incubator/protobuf gRPC northbound service GrpcNbComponentConfigService (lines 113-132).
rejected_leads.reason: The protobuf NB services are exercised through InProcessServer (test/local use) in this snapshot; no evidence of a remote network-exposed gRPC listener.

summary: Scope: the assigned ONOS 1.14.0-SNAPSHOT tree (8,032 readable files; tests stripped — no src/test trees exist; core/store/dist is referenced by core/store/pom.xml but absent from the snapshot). I reviewed the REST/web layer (web/api, web/gui, web/gui2, app WAB web.xml auth constraints), archive/application installation, YANG subsystem, command execution sinks, TLS/trust code, deserialization/Kryo usage, SSRF sinks and the P1 relation index (navigation hints only, no dataflow). The strongest defensible issue is a classic Zip Slip in the core application installer (core/common ApplicationArchive.expandZippedApplication): ZIP entry names are used to build the output path with no canonical/containment check, and the only filter (isTopLevel) inspects the file-name suffix rather than the directory, so "../" entries escape the per-application directory. A second, same-class flaw exists in the YANG live compiler (apps/yang YangLiveCompilerManager.extractZipArchive, reachable in this snapshot mainly through the onos:compile-model CLI; its REST module apps/yang/web has no pom and is not built), noted as a rejected duplicate lead rather than a second candidate.
